sessionTitle: Build AI-powered collaboration on a visual canvas

announcements.name: Text-to-diagram generation in Lucidchart
announcements.shortDescription: The Lucid AI Prompt Editor turns pasted prompts into diagrams placed inside assisted-layout containers that auto-rearrange arrows as shapes are moved.
announcements.longDescription: Lucid's AI tool lets users create diagrams straight from text prompts via the Lucid AI Prompt Editor at the top left, where pasted context generates a logical flowchart with if/then branches. The output is placed in a default assisted-layout container so shapes can be edited and moved while arrows rearrange themselves automatically. A toolbar also lets users add, remove, or change nodes and decision branches without manual work.

announcements.name: Broad diagram-type support
announcements.shortDescription: Generation covers BPMN choreography and sequence diagrams, ERDs, network diagrams, AWS/Azure/Google Cloud architecture diagrams, and UML class diagrams.
announcements.longDescription: Lucid's AI diagramming supports a wide range of diagram types beyond flowcharts, including BPMN choreography and sequence diagrams (demonstrated with a loan application process), ERDs for data engineers who can paste high-level instructions or code, and network diagrams that logically group items like PCs and switches into containers. It also supports basic AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud architecture diagrams, plus UML class and sequence diagrams. All of these are placed into assisted-layout containers so shapes can be moved and arrows rearrange automatically.

announcements.name: Lucid AI in the Lucidspark whiteboard
announcements.shortDescription: AI powers mind-map expansion, idea/sticky-note generation, sorting, and board summarization for collaborative ideation.
announcements.longDescription: Lucid AI in the Lucidspark whiteboard tool focuses on idea generation, starting with the Mindmap widget that can expand on ideas from a topic and keep branching into sub-topics. The Lucid AI Brainstorm tool's Generate Ideas section can produce sets of sticky notes and generate further ideas based on a selected note. Users can also take existing sticky notes and summarize them or sort them into high-level categories using the Sort tool.

announcements.name: Lucid MCP server
announcements.shortDescription: An MCP server lets AI agents search, fetch, summarize, share, and create Lucid diagrams, with more tools described as coming in the pipeline.
announcements.longDescription: With Lucid's MCP server, AI agents can easily search, fetch, summarize, share, and create Lucid diagrams, with many more AI tools described as coming in the pipeline. Example use cases include funneling a meeting conference transcript into Lucid to build a process diagram, ideating with an LLM to design a workshop and create a Lucidspark board shared only with attendees, and connecting an agent to do a system check or sync updates between code and diagrams. The speaker then demonstrates a specific example using a code-based BPMN converter from GitHub that needs review by the security compliance team.

announcements.name: Process agent ("Build A Process")
announcements.shortDescription: A new conversational agent that ingests text, files, or voice-to-text, asks clarifying questions, and builds a first-draft flowchart with swim lanes.
announcements.longDescription: Lucid's brand new process agent, available from the AI jumping-off point under "Build A Process," offers a more conversational experience than traditional Lucid AI. Users describe their process by pasting text such as a standard operating procedure, adding files, or using voice-to-text to capture a rough-draft prompt, and the AI fills in the gaps. The process agent works through the supplied information, may ask clarifying questions about forgotten details, and helps generate a well-thought-out flowchart along with a summary of what it has done.
